offers._note: Spec 1.6 §12: an offer comes when the player's team beats its board target (deserved constructors' rank) by beatBy places, or the player wins the drivers' title; the offering team is stepUp places higher by effective rating.

sprint._note: Sprint weekends (spec 2026-10-16 §3). rounds are 1-based. seedSalt separates the sprint's seed stream from the Grand Prix's; see seedFor in src/state/seasonStore.ts.

setup._note: Wing level 1-5 per car; d=(w-3)/2. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-09-car-setup-design.md section 2. Values measured against spec section 5 in MODEL_SPEC.md section 13 (scripts/calibrate-setup.ts).

timeOfDay._note: Spec 2026-10-24 §2.2. Multiplies effective tyre age at circuits with timeOfDay 'night'. Ships at 1.0 in Task 1 (no effect); Task 5 switches it on and re-measures.

_regressionBands._note: Bands and their provenance live in MODEL_SPEC.md section 3; the staging table is section 4. STAGED (these are the today values, NOT the targets -- do not read a staged floor as a goal): topTeamWinRate, minDistinctWinners, meanAbsPosChange, gridFinishSpearman. The competitive-grid plan has LANDED: it tightened topTeamWinRate to [0.35, 0.90] -- the ceiling is the staged value and the floor is section 3's FINAL target floor, adopted early because a 0.0 floor makes the assertion unfailable (real F1's own minimum is 35.0%, 2012); measured 0.8458 pro / 0.8812 rookie over all 12 circuits, so the floor has ~20pp of headroom and only trips on an overshoot into lottery territory, minDistinctWinners to 4, and -- unpredicted by the staging table -- reached the FINAL section 3 band for gridFinishSpearman, which is therefore now [0.60, 0.80] (measured 0.7357-0.7593 over six n=240 pro samples; the old 0.78 floor was no longer satisfiable and the net change is a tightening, 0.90 -> 0.80 ceiling). meanAbsPosChange has been ADVANCED to its final section 3 band [2.5, 4.0] by the overtaking-race-time plan, on measurement: durable overtaking raised it to 2.9896 +- 0.0428 pro on the 4-circuit gated sample (n=240) and 2.8140 +- 0.0292 pro over all 12 circuits, so the gated sample clears the 2.5 floor by 8 SE at the n=120 the assertion runs at. One caveat on the record: ROOKIE over all 12 circuits measures 2.5812 +- 0.0281, only 2.9 naive SE above the floor, and the harness's SE is known to understate -- if a rookie meanAbsPosChange assertion is ever added it must not use this band without re-measuring. The race-incidents plan still tightens topTeamWinRate's CEILING to 0.55 (the floor is already there). FINAL, not staged: minPaceRankCorrelation, and mechanicalDnfPerCarRace which is section 3's real-F1 band that the sim does NOT currently meet (measures 4.67% +- 0.12pp over 28,800 car-races, 11 SE below the 0.06 floor) -- its assertion is skipped and owned by the race-incidents plan. The circuit-sensitivity plan (2026-08-23) re-measured every band over all 12 circuits at n=720 on two seed bases, both difficulties, and MOVED NOTHING: top-team win share 0.567/0.592 pro and 0.642/0.600 rookie (inside the staged 0.90, still above the final 0.55, which stays with the race-incidents plan), distinct winners 7, meanAbsPosChange 2.863/2.837 pro and 2.618/2.581 rookie (the rookie margin over the 2.5 floor improved from 2.9 to 3.6 naive SE), gridFinishSpearman 0.750/0.756 pro and 0.777/0.787 rookie -- watch that ceiling, rookie's 0.7874 leaves 0.0126 against an observed between-sample spread of 0.010 -- paceRankCorrelation unmoved at 0.9636/0.9152, mechanical DNF 4.51-5.06% and still skipped. Never loosen a gate that has already been met, and never widen a band to make a skipped test pass. The race-incidents plan LANDED 2026-08-29: driverErrorPerLap 0 -> 0.0105, the two safety-car deploy chances 0 -> 0.30/0.12, and mechanicalFailure.baseChancePerLap 0.008 -> 0.012 (the spec proposed 0.014; 0.012 was the owner's choice because it ALSO satisfies the reliability spec's per-team DNF targets -- see MODEL_SPEC.md section 4). Measured over all 12 circuits at n=720, both difficulties, two seed bases: mechanical DNF 7.04-7.42% (IN BAND -- its assertion is now UN-SKIPPED against the same unwidened 0.06-0.10), crashes 6.32-6.54pp (new band 0.05-0.09, anchored to section 3's 7.0pp real-F1 accident share), safety cars 0.518-0.553/race (new band 0.40-0.90, wide because the rate is a product of four inputs), meanAbsPosChange 3.58-3.62 pro and 3.43-3.44 rookie (in band, now nearer the 4.0 CEILING), gridFinishSpearman 0.628-0.636 pro and 0.651-0.654 rookie (in band; the rookie CEILING worry recorded above is resolved, a mild floor margin of 0.039 replaces it), paceRankCorrelation UP to 0.9879/0.9394. TOP-TEAM WIN SHARE WAS NOT MET AND DID NOT MOVE: 56.8-58.8% against the 0.35-0.55 target, from 56.7-59.2% before. Its ceiling therefore STAYS at 0.90 and was deliberately NOT advanced to 0.55 -- advancing it would red the suite on a target no landed mechanism reaches. The reason is structural and is written up in MODEL_SPEC.md sections 4 and 7: the concentration is a DRIVER-pace effect and incidents are driver-agnostic (d_voss alone wins 55.0% of races, two drivers take 86.2%, and drivers.json has a pace cliff at 96/94 then 90/86/85). The magnitudes were not moved in either direction to chase the band, per the spec's section 2.1. Overtake event counts are deliberately NOT banded -- see MODEL_SPEC.md section 5. THE WIN-SHARE PLAN LANDED 2026-09-12 and topTeamWinRate is now [0.35, 0.55]: the LAST staged ceiling reaches its section 3 target. The lever was NOT flattening the leader. Lowering Voss (96->92/93) does hit the band on the 12-circuit calendar but FAILS the 4-circuit gate sample the tests actually assert on -- top-team share fell to 0.317 (below the 0.35 floor) and gridFinishSpearman to 0.584 (below its 0.60 floor), because Plan A's incidents had already spent the rho budget, leaving only 0.013 of headroom above that floor. Compressing the top TEAM's car is worse still: apex at k=0.6/0.3 drops paceRankCorrelation to 0.891/0.794, red-lining its FINAL 0.90 gate. What worked was RAISING THE CHALLENGERS, which widens the top instead of compressing the field: Rossi 94->96 (a genuine equal to Voss), Berg 90->93, Silva 85->88, with potentials lifted to stay above pace. Voss keeps his 96. Measured over 10 seed bases per cell, both difficulties, on BOTH the 12-circuit calendar (n=720) and the 4-circuit gate sample (n=240): top-team share 0.396-0.489 (was 0.550-0.617), distinct winners >=6, and three metrics IMPROVED rather than degrading -- gridFinishSpearman 0.622-0.691 (was 0.613-0.628), paceRankCorrelation min 0.9394 on the calendar (was 0.9152), meanAbsPosChange max 3.650 (was 3.663). Tightest remaining margin is paceRankCorrelation at +0.0152 on the rookie gate sample. Incident rates are untouched: crashes 0.0608-0.0696, safety cars 0.481-0.564, mechanical DNF 0.0642-0.0737, all still in band. 1.5 (2026-10-16): vscPerRace and aiNeutralisationStopsPerRace added, sized as [floor(0.7 x min), ceil(1.3 x max)] to 0.05 over four n=240 cells (pro/rookie x seed bases 1000/7000) on the 4-circuit sample; measured values in MODEL_SPEC.md section 3. 1.6 (2026-10-17): aiWeatherStopsPerRace added, measured on the five showery circuits (bengaluru, harbour_lights, highland, aurora, kaido), same sizing rule; values in MODEL_SPEC.md section 3. slowStopsPerRace added (1.6 §1), 4-circuit sample, same rule. redFlagPerRace added (1.6 §4, crashChance 0.05), 4-circuit sample, same rule; gated at n=240 because the rate is ~0.06/race.
